Lesson 4 · Business route

Regression as an explicit approximation

How should a workshop forecast completion time for a new batch?

What the data show

A straight-line fit estimates 7.23 additional minutes per unit of batch size. The operations team then checks how forecast errors change for larger batches.

What would you decide?

Inspect the curve and residuals, then compare candidate forecasts on held-out data. Choose the level of complexity that improves the decision, not merely the training score.

Pause and explain

Does a high in-sample fit make the line a reliable forecast for very large batches?

Compare your reasoning

No. The generating mean bends, and prediction beyond the observed size range needs a separate argument.

Check your judgment

Reveal the case’s known answer

The case’s completion-time curve bends as batches grow, and larger batches have more variable completion times. A size-based rule needs a buffer for deadline promises.

Continue at your own depth

Read the guided lesson

The guided lesson follows this business decision through the practical problem, evidence and next action. The technical appendix has the generation rules, derivations and all 24 original teaching stops.
